shower.thought: # Shower Thoughts
We spend our whole lives learning how to be human, but nobody tells us we've been doing it since birth.
The people who hurt you most are often just people who were hurt first and never learned how to put it down.
You've probably had the same conversation with different people a hundred times, each one thinking they were the only one having it with you.
Nostalgia is just your brain cherry-picking evidence that you were happier, even though you were probably just younger.
We call it "falling in love" as if it's accidental, but we spend years trying to trip ourselves into it.
The scariest part of growing up isn't that you make mistakes—it's that you start recognizing the same mistakes in people older than you.
You only realize how much time you wasted when you finally run out of it.
The people who give the best advice are usually the ones still figuring out how to follow it themselves.
We treat our bodies like we'll trade them in for new ones later, but we only get the one.
Most of what you worry about never happens, but the one thing that does is always something you never saw coming.
Forgiveness isn't about letting someone off the hook—it's about taking the knife out of your own back.
The moments that change your life are usually the ones you don't recognize until years later.
We're all just trying to prove something to someone who probably stopped watching a long time ago.
The people you miss most are usually the ones you took for granted while they were still here.
You can't think your way out of a feeling, but you keep trying anyway.
The hardest part of being honest with others is realizing how dishonest you've been with yourself.
We say "I'm fine" so often that we forget what fine actually feels like.
The void you're trying to fill might not be asking for something—maybe it's asking you to stop running from nothing.
You become your parents not by making the same mistakes, but by recognizing them too late to stop.

The discipline you build today becomes the freedom you enjoy tomorrow. — Unknown

darkjoke.thought: I told my girlfriend she was drawing her eyebrows too high. She looked surprised.
My grandfather said "your generation is too reliant on technology." I agreed while googling how to perform CPR.
I have the memory of an elephant. Which is great, except elephants never forget, so I still remember every embarrassing thing I've ever done.
My therapist asked what my biggest fear was. I said, "Unused potential." She said that ship has sailed.
I'm reading a book on the history of glue. Can't put it down.
My friend said he was going to commit suicide. I said, "You're just going through a phase." Turns out he was.
I donated my body to science. They immediately asked for a refund.
My dating profile says I'm fluent in sarcasm. Apparently that's not the personality trait I think it is.
I told my kids the tooth fairy wasn't real. My wife said I ruined their childhood. I said, "Someone had to."
People keep telling me I'm too hard on myself. I disagree. I'm exactly hard enough.
My doctor said I needed to watch my drinking. So now I drink in front of a mirror.
I'm not saying I'm depressed, but I've started meal-prepping my sadness for the week.
My mother-in-law said, "One day you'll understand what it means to be a parent." She was right. That day was yesterday, and I regret everything.
I asked the crematorium if they offered a loyalty program. Turns out they do—after nine bodies, the tenth is free.
My job is so soul-crushing, my therapist asked if I'd considered quitting. I said, "Daily." She said, "No, I meant therapy."
I love my wife. I love her so much I've started a countdown to retirement, and we're not even close.
My friend asked why I never smile in photos. I said, "Resting bitch face runs in my family." Turns out it runs faster than I do.
I told my boss I was having an existential crisis. He said, "Not on company time."
My hobbies include making terrible life choices and documenting them for future regret.
I'm not antisocial. I just think people are exhausting, and silence is a love language.
